info.title: qbt backtest service
info.description: Submit backtests of the qbt strategies and poll for their results. Jobs run on workers in the background, at least once and deterministically. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details.

get.description: The strategies POST /backtests accepts, with their parameter schemas.

200 if this process can run a query on the database (SELECT 1),
else 503. The container healthcheck (python -m qbt_service.health
api) calls this.

value.detail: The database could not be reached. Nothing was changed unless a retry says otherwise: retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

post.description:
Validates the request, picks the newest price snapshot that covers
[start, end), and queues a job. Returns 202 at once; poll
GET /backtests/{id} for the outcome.

`params` is checked against the strategy's schema (GET /strategies),
and omitted fields take their defaults. The stored request has
every default filled in, and two requests that validate to the
same values are the same request for the Idempotency-Key.

Idempotency (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header): with
an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry of the same request returns the same
job with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different
request gets 422 (`/problems/idempotency-key-reused`). 409, which
the draft uses for a retry while the original is still being
processed, can't happen: the job is created atomically, and a
concurrent retry waits for it and then replays it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Makes the POST safe to retry: the same key with the same request returns the original job instead of creating another. A Structured Field String ("...", as in the IETF draft) or the bare value; 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters. Optional.

get.description:
The job's status, attempts, timestamps and last error, the request
as stored, and, once it has succeeded, its metrics and run details.

A job can go back from `running` to `queued`: a failed attempt that
will be retried, or a worker that died or shut down. `attempts`
counts attempts started; `last_error` says why the previous one
ended.

get.description:
The equity curve, drawdown and position of a succeeded job, day by
day, as stored when it ran. Read-only: nothing is recomputed except
the drawdown (from the stored equity) and, for a learning strategy,
its first out-of-sample day (from the job's stored price snapshot
and params, exactly as the worker loaded them).

post.description:
Scores a model version (the latest unless `version` is given) on the
latest complete month in its pinned price snapshot (`as_of`), i.e.
forecasts the month after as_of. That month's label isn't in the
snapshot, so the model never trained on it. Every prediction is
logged, and every response carries the model's out-of-sample
accuracy and the baseline it was measured against.

strategy_version.description: The strategy's behaviour version this job was submitted to (and, once it has run, ran with). A job whose version is no longer current is failed rather than run with newer code; resubmit it.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: full_report() metrics, once succeeded; otherwise null. A value that is NaN (e.g. a Sharpe ratio with no variance) is null.

strategy_version.title: Strategy Version

equity.title: Equity
equity.description: Growth of 1 after costs: the curve the job's metrics are computed on.

drawdown.title: Drawdown
drawdown.description: (equity - running peak) / running peak, from qbt.analytics.drawdown_series: 0 at a new high, negative below it. Its minimum is the job's `max_drawdown` metric.

position.title: Position
position.description: The position held on each day: the signal shifted one day, so a decision at one close earns from the next (0 = flat, 1 = long).

out_of_sample_from.title: Out Of Sample From
out_of_sample_from.description: For a strategy that learns from history (ml_direction): its first out-of-sample day. It holds no position before it (its training period), and the job's metrics cover the FULL period, those flat training days included. Null for a strategy that learns nothing: every day is out of sample.

SmaCrossoverParams.title: SmaCrossoverParams
SmaCrossoverParams.description: Goes long when the short moving average is above the long one, flat otherwise. The two averages are a crude trend filter: the short one tracks recent price, the long one tracks the established level, and the crossover is the moment recent price decisively left the old level behind.
